rationale: This is a mechanical triple-MIN stacking of two already-archived conditional signals (Depreciation-Honest Earnings Value and Binding Accrual-Overhang Value) with no new mechanism, and the extra hard gate will mostly shrink the effective long tail rather than add information.

The rank×z-score construction is internally consistent with the negative expected sign (loss firms with high overhang score highest, low-overhang loss firms lowest) and is a genuine diagnostic response to the prior conjunction's weak alpha, though it inherits the same rank-times-z-score architecture that already failed on the cash-flow/payables channel.

This is effectively a re-specification of the archived Under-Depreciation Book Trap (B/M times falling depreciation intensity), which already delivered a wrong-signed alpha, and the stated motivation cites a different archived signal rather than confronting that direct precedent.

The hypothesis asks only for absence of sales contraction, but the MIN gate on IND_RANK of sales growth requires top-ranked sales expansion to score highly, which both misstates the expression and pushes the long leg toward high sales growth — a well-documented negative return predictor working against the value leg.

Swapping MIN for SUMRANK on the identical two channels of Persistent Inventory Funding Trap is an aggregation tweak rather than a substantively different mechanism, and it will not fix the coverage problem since both legs are still required, in a channel that has now produced near-zero Fama-MacBeth slopes across four archived variants.

Applying a two-period moving average to the quality leg of the archived Depreciation-Covered Cash Value is a cosmetic smoothing variant of an already-strong signal, unlikely to constitute a distinct economic test.
